sources.claim: Route parameters and search values are untrusted URL strings that need decoding, validation, defaults, and canonicalization.

canonicalExplanation.summary: Route parameters (`/courses/:courseId`) and search values (`?page=2&level=beginner`) come from the **address bar**, so anyone can type anything. They're always **strings** (or null when missing), and they're **untrusted**. Read them with `useParams()` and `useSearchParams()`, then **parse, validate and default**: turn "2" into the number 2, reject "-5" or "abc", fall back to page 1. When a value is invalid, show a sensible default or a not-found view, and consider **replacing** the URL with the canonical one so it can be shared correctly.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A course list uses `?page=` for pagination. Someone shares `?page=-3`, another link has `?page=abc`, and the list shows "Page NaN of 12" with no results. A numeric page parameter is parsed, range-checked, and replaced with a safe default when invalid. In this lesson you'll implement and test parameterized and filterable views with invalid and unknown URLs.

examples.title: The page number nobody checked
examples.situation: A numeric page parameter is parsed, range-checked, and replaced with a safe default when invalid.
walkthrough: **Range-check:** parsePage accepts only whole numbers from 1 to totalPages, otherwise returns 1.
**Test:** unit tests will call parsePage with "2", null, "abc", "-3" and "99" and expect 2, 1, 1, 1 and 1.
examples.result: Any page value in a shared link shows a real page instead of "Page NaN".

examples.title: The course that crashed on a typo
examples.situation: Visiting `/courses/csss` throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'title')" and shows a blank screen.
walkthrough: courseId "csss" matched the route but no course.
The component used the lookup result without checking it.
Fix: if the course isn't found, render a not-found view with a link to all courses.
examples.result: Mistyped course links show a friendly not-found page.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: A typed route declaration guarantees every parameter value is valid domain data.
misconceptions.correction: URL parameters are strings typed by people and shared by links. A type only describes shape; the component must parse, validate and handle missing or unknown values.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The page number nobody checked", what did "abc" become?

analogy.example: URL parameters are like **handwritten order slips**. The form has a box for "quantity", but people write "two", "-3" or leave it blank. A good shop reads the slip, checks it makes sense, and uses a sensible default, rather than trusting the box's label.
limitations: Slips can't be edited after sending; URLs can be replaced.
An unknown product code is a not-found case, not a crash.

steps.explanation: The search value arrives as an untrusted string.
The numeric page parameter is parsed, range-checked, and replaced with a safe default.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing an invalid page value. Step 1, Read: params.get('page') is 'abc'. The search value arrives as an untrusted string. Step 2, Validate: Number('abc') is NaN; page is 1. nearTransfer.prompt: Add a `sort` search value that accepts only "title" or "newest" (default "newest"), and update the URL when the learner changes the sort select.
expectedEvidence: Invalid sort falls back to newest.

farTransfer.prompt: Build a lesson page at `/courses/:courseId/lessons/:n` where n is a lesson number. Handle invalid numbers, out-of-range numbers and unknown courses, and write tests for each URL.
scaffold: Not-found view with a link back.
expectedEvidence: Tests for valid, invalid, out-of-range and unknown.

remediation.explanation: For each value from the URL write: **raw string → parsed value → valid range or allow-list → default or not-found.** Test at least one missing, one malformed and one out-of-range value.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The course that crashed on a typo".

recap.summary: To implement and test parameterized and filterable views, read params and search values as untrusted strings, parse and range-check or allow-list them, fall back to safe defaults, write canonical values back to the URL, and show a not-found view for unknown items instead of crashing.
